draft.title: Probabilities from the normal distribution
card: Step 1: turn each end of the interval into a z-score using z = (x − μ)/σ. Step 2: use the z-scores to find the area under the standard normal curve. That area is the probability.
Empirical rule
About 68% of values lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean, 95% within 2 and 99.7% within 3. The curve is symmetric, so half of the area lies on each side of the mean.
Table or calculator
A z-table gives P(Z ≤ z). For an interval, P(a < Z < b) = P(Z ≤ b) − P(Z ≤ a). For a value above z, P(Z > z) = 1 − P(Z ≤ z).
Example

Heights have μ = 170 and σ = 10. For 150 to 190, z = −2 to 2, so P is about 0.95. For above 180, z = 1. Within 1 standard deviation is 68%, so the two tails share 32%. Each tail is 16%, so P(X > 180) is about 0.16.
draft.remember: Convert to z-scores, then read the area from the empirical rule or a table.

a.q: Test marks are normal with mean 60 and standard deviation 8. What is the approximate probability that a mark is between 44 and 76?
a.why: z = (44 − 60)/8 = −2 and z = (76 − 60)/8 = 2. The interval is within 2 standard deviations of the mean, so the probability is about 0.95. The value 0.68 is for 1 standard deviation, not 2.
a.clue: Find the z-scores of 44 and 76 first.

b.q: The lifetime of a battery is normal with mean 400 hours and standard deviation 25 hours. What is the approximate probability that a battery lasts more than 450 hours?
b.why: z = (450 − 400)/25 = 2. About 95% of values lie within 2 standard deviations, so 5% lie outside, split equally between the two tails. The upper tail is 0.025. The value 0.05 is wrong because it counts both tails.
b.clue: The 95% from the empirical rule covers both tails, but this question asks about one.

problems.detail: The clue says 'The 95% from the empirical rule covers both tails', which is wrong: the 95% is the middle area within 2 standard deviations, and the remaining 5% is what is shared between the two tails. Reword it, for example: 'The 5% outside 2 standard deviations is split between both tails, but this question asks about one.'

check.summary: Both questions and the card are correct (a: 0.95, b: 0.025). The clue for question b wrongly says the 95% covers both tails, when it is the 5% outside that is split between the tails.
